title: $:/plugins/wikilabs/viewportobserver
author: pmario
name: Viewport Observer
description: Eventcatcher that also runs actions when elements enter or leave the viewport
readme:
The `<$viewportobserver>` widget is an [[EventCatcherWidget|https://tiddlywiki.com/#EventCatcherWidget]] that can also run actions when elements enter or leave the viewport. It accepts every attribute of the eventcatcher, plus: |!Attribute |!Description | |$enterview |Actions run when an element matching `selector` scrolls into the viewport | |$leaveview |Actions run when an element that was in the viewport leaves it | |rootMargin |Grows or shrinks the viewport, like CSS margin, e.g. `300px` to start early (default `0px`) | |threshold |Visible fraction that counts as "in view", one or more numbers between 0 and 1 (default `0`) | |lazy |`yes` renders the content only when the widget's own element first comes into view (default `no`) | Without `selector`, the widget's own element is observed. The actions get the same `dom-*` variables as the eventcatcher actions, plus `event-type` (`enterview` or `leaveview`) and `intersection-ratio`. Example: collect the titles of the rows that were scrolled into view. ``` \procedure seenActions() <$action-listops $tiddler="$:/temp/volatile/seen" $subfilter="[]"/> \end <$viewportobserver selector=".row" rootMargin="300px" $enterview=<>> <$list filter="[tag[Rows]]">
>><$link/>
``` Writing to a `$:/temp/volatile/` tiddler delays the refresh until scrolling pauses, so a fast scroll causes one refresh instead of many. Example: render expensive content only when it is about to scroll into view. `lazy` renders in place and changes no tiddler, so the rest of the page does not refresh. ``` <$list filter="[tag[Rows]]"> <$viewportobserver lazy="yes" rootMargin="200% 0px"> <> ``` All widgets with the same `rootMargin` and `threshold` share one browser observer. Where the browser has no `IntersectionObserver`, e.g. when TiddlyWiki renders on Node.js, the view actions never run and `lazy` content renders at once.
